summary: A cast-iron 'sparkplug' light of 1890 in the Lubec Channel at Lubec, Maine; automated in 1939 and sold to a private owner in 2007.

lens.note: USLHS: original fourth-order Fresnel, installed 1890. New England Lighthouses says fifth-order. Current optic: solar-powered LED (VLB-44), installed 2017 (USLHS).

fog_signal.note: Board notice sets 31 Jan 1891; New England Lighthouses dates the 1,200-lb bell to 1890. Station record gives a horn today.

structures.note: Cast-iron caisson filled with concrete, sunk 6 ft into the site, topped by an iron tower 37 ft to focal plane (1890 Board report as quoted by NE). USLHS: 40 ft base to lantern centre.

access.note: USLHS: owner 'Private owner'; 'Open to Public: No'. Base stands in the channel, so approach is by water.

visit.note: Private property; not open to the public (USLHS).

events.note: Light-House Board report notes the need for a light in the channel (NRHP)
Congress appropriates $40,000 for the lighthouse (New England Lighthouses)
29 Aug 1889: water bursts in through the subsoil inside the caisson and stops work; 185 spruce piles added as a sub-foundation (NE)
Fog bell, struck by machinery a single blow every ten seconds, from 31 January 1891 (Board notice)
Two inclined ladders replaced by two vertical iron ladders bolted to the pier
Keeper James W. Doran assisted a disabled power boat near the light, 25 November; year inferred from the Bulletin issue of 2 January 1925
Keeper Nathaniel S. Alley overcome by coal-stove fumes on 7 March 1934, taken to Lubec and died there (New England Lighthouses only)
Acetylene gas system with a sun valve (NE); USLHS year automated 1939
Discontinuance planned; 'Save the Sparkplug' campaign by local residents (NE)
$700,000 renovation: foundation stabilized, new plates on the caisson, concrete pumped in (NE)
Sold by auction in July 2007 for a high bid of $46,000, after no applicants under the 2000 Act
Current optic: VLB-44 LED, solar powered (USLHS)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. USLHS roster: first assistant 1890-1895, principal 1895-1923 (28 years as principal). New England Lighthouses: principal from 1898. Eastport dispatch (1923): service from 1881, 32 years as keeper. The story reports all three.

USLHS roster (from NARA registers) gives Morong 1890-1895 and Myers principal from 1895. New England Lighthouses gives Morong 1890-1898 and Myers principal from 1898. The story uses the roster and reports the other date.
USLHS gives fourth-order Fresnel; New England Lighthouses gives fifth-order. Reported in the story; not resolved.

notes_for_editor: 1) Wikipedia (read for leads only, not cited) gives automation 1968 and a horn fog signal; NRHP and USLHS give 1939. 2) New England Lighthouses (source 10) is the only source for: the 1889-1890 construction details (the Board's 1890 report as quoted there, not checked against the report, which is not in the corpus), the fifth-order lens, the 1,200-lb bell, the 1898 promotion, Abbie Myers's 1899 service, the 1904 lifeboat, Alley's 1934 death, the 1989-1992 history and the 2007 buyer (not named in the story). The site is copyrighted: the story paraphrases and quotes only short phrases. Check the 1890 Light-House Board annual report for the caisson description and lens order. 3) Myers's service: roster 28 years as principal; dispatch 32 years as keeper and service from 1881; NE 1898 promotion. Unresolved, all stated. 4) Site: the 1923 dispatch says 'a sandbar'; NRHP says 'a submerged rock ledge'. Stated in the story. 5) Alley's death (7 Mar 1934) is not in the Chronicling America search for 'Lubec Channel' and 'Alley' in 1934 (no hits), and the 1930-35 Bulletin index does not list him. Single-source; check the 1934 Bulletin text and Maine papers before publication. 6) Abbie Myers is not on the roster and is single-source (NE). The story says so. 7) The 1894 Light-House Board note (p. 312, scan 721) is badly OCR'd; quotes were copied from the OCR text, and the keeper's remarks are paraphrased. The report's index lists 'Lubec Channel, Maine, observations 312', which supports p. 312. 8) 1899 repairs: cited by scan page 74; printed page not read. 9) Bulletin 2 Jan 1925: the item gives '25 November' with no year. 1924 is inferred from the issue date and flagged in the events and wreck entries. 10) The record's characteristic (Fl W 6s) and range (6 nm) are not verified from a source read here, so they are omitted from facts. Check the Coast Guard Light List. NE gives the first characteristic as a white flash every 15 seconds, not verified. 11) The record gives a horn fog signal; the 1891 and 1894 sources describe a bell. Not checked whether the bell was replaced. 12) Quoddy Tides (qdy.stparchive.com) returned HTTP 403; Lighthouse Digest pages are not readable in full. 13) Position: the record's OSM point is about 140 m from the USLHS position (44.8417, -66.9783, given to the tenth of a minute); the record was not changed. 14) USLHS roster lines matched by name and position (0.13 km).
